On campus housing can be high in demand, limited and the allocation is based on 1st come 1st serve – on the date when the student answered the housing question. Deakin request Students to register and submit their Housing preference via the online application system early.

program_information_raw: At Deakin there are many different schools and faculties. You can for instance find courses at the: School of Communication and Creative Arts, School of Humanities and Social Sciences, Deakin Graduate School of Business, School of Accounting, Economics and Finance, School of Information and Business Analytics, School of Law, School of Management and Marketing, School of Psychology, School of Information Technology etc. To find the undergraduate courses please take a look at the online hand book here Any unit which starts with 1,2,3 or 4 is an undergraduate unit. For information on unit choices and availability for 2019, please visit http://www.deakin.edu.au/students/enrolment-fees-and-money/university-handbook/2019-handbook For Arts units enter A into the search function, M for Business and Law, S for Science and Technology, E for Education and H for Health. Pre-approved Units (Subjects): Deakin also have a list of Pre-Approved Units , that do not require to go for assessment to the Deakin Faculty’s– which can add time. Choosing units from this list, can assist in faster processing.
additional_information_raw: Deakin offers a unique three day beach welcome introduction program (for a small fee) . It is set in a picturesque seaside town and designed specifically for Exchange and Study Abroad students to make the transition into Australian university life as easy as possible. Students have the chance to participate in iconic Australian pastimes such as learning to surf and play Australian Rules Football or just sit back and watch the waves roll in. Deakin is very committed to engaging in local communities in diverse ways and as such we have a new unit on offer which exchange students are encouraged to undertake. The unit is MIS291 - Community Based Volunteering and it gives students the opportunity to gain credit for volunteering . For information please follow the link http://www.deakin.edu.au/buslaw/wil/cbv.php More information about exchange at Deakin: http://www.deakin.edu.au/international-students/study-abroad-and-exchange
info_about_university_raw: Deakin is a multi-award winning university with an international focus. They are young and innovative offering excellent facilities and flexible learning. Deakin is Australia's 9th largest university with over 42,000 students, of whom approximately a fifth are international students from over 100 different countries. You can find a lot of information about exchange at Deakin in their study brochure here Deakin university is spread out over four different campuses: Melbourne Burwood, Warrnambool and two in Geelong. The campus CBS students go to is usually the Melbourne campus at Burwood. The Burwood campus is located around 45-60 minutes from the city center by tram. Their campuses have cafes and eateries where you can socialise and relax. There are also many clubs and societies that allow you to expand your interests and make new friends. Deakin Business School is AACSB accredited.

info_about_university_raw: Since opening its doors in 1975, Griffith University has come to be regarded as one of Australia's most innovative tertiary institutions. It was the first university in Australia to offer degrees in Asian studies and Environmental studies and they remain pioneers in these fields. It is a large multi-campus institution with internationally recognised strengths in teaching and research. Griffith offers more than 300 degrees across five campuses and is home to more than 43,000 students from 131 countries. Campuses at Southbank, Nathan, Mt Gravatt, Logan and the Gold Coast, swathed in sub-tropical sunshine, feature many state-of-the art facilities that reflect the university's innovation and future focus. Home to world-class expertise in the environment, corporate sustainability, Asia and the emerging bio-sciences, Nathan is the original Griffith campus. With more than 13,900 students and situated in tranquil, native bushland on the edge of Toohey Forest, Nathan campus is a short walk or bus ride from our Mt Gravatt campus or a 25 minute bus ride from central Brisbane. Public transport connects the campus to Mt Gravatt, Garden City shopping centre and the Brisbane CBD. There is a new lightrail (a tram called G-link) connecting the Gold Coast campus with the main Gold Coast area/town and Surfer's Paradise. Griffith University is AACSB accredited.

additional_information_raw: It is possible to combine your studies with a practical placement such as a Sport Management Project or a Media Studies Internship. Please note that the internships are subject to availability in any given semester. La Trobe also offer a volunteer program at the Melbourne Wildlife Sanctuary. Find out more at latrobe.edu.au/wildlife The university also offer a Pre-Orientation trip. Destination: Great Ocean Road for a weekend. It is a great opportunity to make new friends and get used to the Aussie way of living.
info_about_university_raw: In 1967, 552 students enrolled at La Trobe University, the third University to open in Victoria. It has grown to accommodate more than 34,000 students including approximately 8,000 international students. There is now a network of campuses and around 24,000 students are studying at the Melbourne campus. At La Trobe you will find world-class teaching and academic excellence, stunning native Australian campus environments and lots of extracurricular trips and activities. The Bundoora campus is located 14 km from the city center of Melbourne. It takes approximately 40 minutes to 1 hour to reach La Trobe with public transportation. La Trobe's Melbourne campus offer 267 hectares of beautiful parkland and waterways including a major wildlife sanctuary (so yes you will see kangaroos on-campus). The campus community feel is completed with retail outlets and services including a bookshop, hairdresser, travel agent, weekly market, banks, bakery, post office, cinema, convenience store and child care. Furthermore, you will find plenty of cafés and restaurants on campus. Finally, there are many sport facilities on-campus.

Macquarie also offer short-term accommodation for those students, who would like to find a place to stay on their own but would like the comfort of having a place to sleep the first few weeks while settling in. A new self-catered college close to campus is also available for exchange students.
course_availability_raw: Access to courses offered by the following faculties: Business & Economics, Human Sciences, Arts, and Science. program_information_raw: At the Faculty of Business and Economics, Macquarie offer courses within: Accounting, Finance, Actuarial Studies, Business and Business Law, Economics, Management, Human Resource Management, Marketing and Commerce At the Faculty of Arts, Macquarie offer, among others, courses within: Asian and European languages, International Studies, Law, Media and Cultural Studies, Politics, International Relations and Security, Sociology, Anthropology and Philosophy Students wishing to see available subjects should consult the Online Handbook , where all units are listed. Those students coming in Session 2, 2016 should ensure that they only choose subjects running in Session 2 - Day or Session 2 - Evening. Please note, some units are restricted and as such, not available to Study Abroad or Exchange students. (please be kindly advised that the newest Handbook will only be available at the beginning of the year you are going on exchange, please use the previous years Handbook as your reference). Restricted units: http://www.mq.edu.au/study/international-students/how-to-apply/study-abroad-and-exchange/restricted-units Additionally, if you would like to view the Unit Outlines (syllabus) for units offered by any Department of the University, please consult the Unit guides: http://unitguides.mq.edu.au/units It is easier to use this once you know the unit codes from the Online Handbook.
additional_information_raw: Macquarie’s Global Leadership Certificate (part of the Global Leadership Program, or GLP) is unique to Macquarie University and provides students with unparalleled opportunities to enhance their Exchange experience, develop important leadership skills and participate in professional development forums. Macquarie’s Global Leadership Certificate has been designed so that you not only learn global skills and understanding – you put them into practice by studying, volunteering and participating in activities in Australia and overseas. Read more here: http://students.mq.edu.au/opportunities/global_leadership_program/ Macquarie offers a program called PACE . It is a program which involves teaching at the university as well as practical experience in a company . Incoming undergraduate exchange students to Macquarie (MQ) can apply to participate in PACE if they have completed at least 39 MQ credits . When you go through the registration process for MQ , you can on the registration form select the " PACE unit" that you are interested in . After that you will get a reply from Macquarie. There is no standard application process as such . There is a great interest in the PACE program and MQ full-degree students have first priority - so there is no guarantee to get into a PACE unit. One PACE unit is worth 3 MQ credits. PACE business units are not open to exchange students but there are options within other study areas. http://www.mq.edu.au/about_us/offices_and_units/professional_and_community_engagement/
info_about_university_raw: Macquarie University was founded in 1964 to be a radical and unconventional addition to the New South Wales tertiary education market. Fifty years on, Macquarie University is still different. Macquarie is proudly a university of service and engagement - engaging students and staff through transformative learning and life experiences, and serving the world through discovery, dissemination of knowledge and ideas, innovation and deep partnerships. Our unique location, in the heart of Australia's largest high-technology precinct, provides benefits for staff and students through an environment of outstanding research and innovation, and through learning and teaching opportunities with world-leading organisations. Macquarie University is one of Australia’s leading universities. The University has been placed in the top 40 in the Asia-Pacific region, and ranked within Australia's top ten universities (international Shanghai Jiao Tong University Rankings, 2012. Macquarie University offers a unique study experience: world-class educational, recreational and research facilities; a spacious parkland campus and all the attractions of living in the cosmopolitan city of Sydney.

housing_raw: On-campus is available. On-campus accommodation options can include fully-catered and non-catered communal living in shared residential halls and colleges, or independent living in self-contained, self-catered units. Exchange students commencing in either semester are welcome to apply for accommodation ab d will be notified by means of an offer if a place becomes available. Students should apply already when sending the exchange application to Monash. All accommodation at Monash, except Caulfield, is co-ed but all students have single rooms. Students who prefer to live off-campus must find their own accommodation but can obtain advice and assistance from Monash Residential Services (MRS). There is a very wide range of shared student accommodation available all over Melbourne, especially near the major universities, and most exchange students are able to find off-campus accommodation. Students who want to live off-campus should be advised to arrive in Melbourne one to two weeks before orientation starts to look for a permanent place to live.

Monash' teachers are experts in the fields of accounting, finance, business law and taxation, econometrics, business statistics, economics, management and marketing. Link to courses: Unit search Search for courses at the Caulfield or Clayton campuses.
additional_information_raw: There is a special enrolment and orientation program conducted by Monash Abroad for exchange students each semester. It is compulsory for all students and takes place approximately ten days before the start of semester (usually in the third week of February and the second week of July). It is essential students arrange travel so that they can attend. The Monash Abroad orientation is separate from the international orientation (for full course international students) and the general university orientation (for all commencing students). Students should ensure they check the correct program on the Monash Abroad www.monash.edu/international/studyabroad/support/ orientation.html
info_about_university_raw: Monash University, established in 1958, is now Australia's largest university with more than 62,000 students. Monash has achieved an enviable national and international reputation for research and teaching excellence in a short 50 years. Monash is ranked in the top 1 per cent of world universities. Monash are a known leader in the education of international students and has more than 21,000 international students and expertise in hosting a range of nationalities. Monash has two main campuses in Melbourne, one in the suburb of Clayton and the other in Caulfield. CBS students usually follow classes at both campuses or only at Caulfield. The Caulfield campus is smaller than Clayton and located closer to the city center of Melbourne (approx. 10 km from the city center). Clayton is located approx. 20 km from the city. The Faculty of Business and Economics is EQUIS, AACSB and AMBA accredited (the so-called Triple Crown Accreditation) and the university is a member of the Group of Eight - a coalition of Australian top research intensive universities.

info_about_university_raw: UQ is Queensland's oldest university and is known for its international reputation for teaching quality and world leading research. It was f ounded in 1910 The University of Queensland (UQ) is one of Australia’s premier learning and research institutions. Internationally renowned for its highly awarded teaching staff, world-class facilities and superior campus environment, 45,400 students, including 11,300 international students from over 135 countries, choose to study at UQ. UQ’s main campus is located in the picturesque inner-city suburb of St Lucia. Bounded by the Brisbane River on three sides, and only seven kilometres from Brisbane’s vibrant city heart, this 285-acre site provides students with the perfect study research and living environment. UQ is a member of Universitas 21, a global alliance that ensures quality university outcomes through international benchmarking. UQ is EQUIS and AACSB accredited and a a member of the Group of Eight- a coalition of Australian top research intensive universities.

info_about_university_raw: Swinburne University of Technology is based in Melbourne, Australia's 2nd largest city. The Good Universities Guide has ranked Swinburne as the best university in Melbourne for teaching quality (2001-2011) and graduate satisfaction (2007, 2008, 2010, 2011). Swinburne has recently been promoted to one of the world's top-400 universities by the Academic Ranking of World Universities. Swinburne is in 2012 therefore ranked number 10 in Australia and among the top-three universities in Melbourne. Established in 1908, Swinburne has been educating students for more than 100 years. Swinburne has three locations around Melbourne but most CBS students study at the Hawthorn campus. It is located in a nice neighbourhood full of shops, cosy cafés and restaurants, and it is only 10 minutes by train from the city center of Melbourne. By choosing to study at Swinburne, you will gain an international perspective with a focus on the practial course content that is the backbone of their academic approach. Swinburne has more than 98 undergraduate and 186 postgraduate programs from which you can choose different courses. At Swinburne you will find almost 30,000 students and over 7,000 international students. Small campus and class environment provides a more personal and supportive study experience and Swinburne offer various university-wide support services including mini trips and activities, sport and recreation and academic support. The Australian Government's Excellence in Research for Australia (ERA) 2012 rated Swinburne as above world standard (ERA 4) for these fields among others: Communication and Media Studies, Computer Software and Psychology. Find more information about Swinburne's exchange program at http://www.international.swinburne.edu.au/study-abroad/incoming/details/index.html

info_about_university_raw: The University of Melbourne is a vibrant institution with a reputation for excellence built over 150 years. Their success has been achieved by insisting on international excellence and among their many scholars of international standing are three winners of the Nobel Prize. The researchers are at the forefront of international scholarship in fields as diverse as human rights, art conservation and nanotechnology. University of Melbourne is ranked the no. 1 university in Australia and ranked no. 28 in the world (according to Times Higher Education rankings). The University is AACSB accredited and a a member of the Group of Eight - a coalition of Australian top research intensive universities. The main Parkville campus is a unique blend of traditional and contemporary culture. It offers students a range of galleries, theatre and entertainment venues, bookshops, retail stores, cafes and restaurants all within walking distance from Melbourne’s city center. Students will find themselves mixing with international students from over 100 countries and our student clubs offer something for everyone. There is also an extensive range of sport and recreational activities.

info_about_university_raw: UTS is an innovative and practice-oriented university with an international outlook. It is located in the heart of Sydney and offer career-relevant education across a diverse range of traditional and emerging fields. UTS' academics are regularly awarded for their achievements. At UTS there is a focus on practive-oriented learning and many of the programs include major projects, case studies, extensive group work and field-trips. UTS offer a wide range of technologically advanced facilities to support the academic, social and sporting life at university. The University welcomes over 300 study abroad and exchange students each semester and is home to over 30,000 students from more than 115 different countries. With spacious and well-equipped student areas, the UTS campus encourages interaction and academic collaboration suitable to their model of learning. Whether for socialising, group meetings or independent study, adaptable indoor and outdoor environments are available and are equipped with power and WIFI access. Additionally, specialised group-work areas offer the latest technologies such as SMART boards, plasma screens and touch screen projectors – which allow you to simply plug in and go. A natural hub for your studies, the UTS Library provides broad ranging academic support with more than 800,000 books, journals, audio visual and online publications. The Library website offers 24-hour global access to their catalogue. more than 1300 computers in 40 locations are available across the university, with 24/7 PIN-access to certain facilities. UTS will soon be home to the first Frank Gehry-designed building in Australia, and a physical symbol of creative thinking in the Sydney central precinct. The campus redevelopment plans also include a new library with an underground automatic resource retrieval system, modern social spaces and brand new buildings for Science, IT and Engineering. UTS School of Business is the largest faculty at UTS and is one of the largest Business Schools in Australia. With almost 11,500 students, over 300 academics and 6 prominent research centres, the School contributes not only highly skilled and knowledgeable graduates to the workforce, but engages in ground breaking research that is changing and shaping the industry. UTS School of Business was ranked #1 in Australia in the Thomson Reuters measure of research impact in Economics and Business over a four year period and is rated “above world standard” and “well above world standard” by the Excellent in Research for Australia (ERA) report across a range or research areas including economics, accounting, auditing, business and management. Through engagement with industry, UTS School of Business maintains its courses up to date using relevant industry benchmarks. Graduates continue to be in demand for their work-ready, creative and sophisticated capabilities. The UTS Business School is AACSB accredited.

Antwerp and its harbor is both cultural and from a business perspective unique. The courses have a more hands-on approach, with slightly less focus on quantitative skills but more on business and management. CAMPUS BURSSELS Campus Brussels has a strong focus on business and management (both Bachelor and Master level entirely in English with additional minors). Brussels also stands for the image of a world city (unofficial capital of the EU, headquarters of Nato, etc.). The courses have a more hands-on approach, with slightly less focus on quantitative skills but more on business and management. CAMPUS LEUVEN Campus Leuven has a smaller offer on the Bachelor level. FEB courses in fields such as economics and finance tend to be very analytical, and students should be well versed in mathematics/statistics. Leuven thrives as a bustling student town with a strong International allure, where various cultures meet and experiences are exchanged. The University is located in Flanders, the Dutch-speaking Nothern part of Belgium. With the Dutch language's steady rise to renewed prominence, 1968 saw the university split into two new universities. The French-speaking Université Catholique de Louvain moved to the newly built campus in Louvain-la-Neuve. The Dutch-speaking Katholieke Universiteit Leuven remained in the historic town of Leuven. The Faculty of Economics and Business of the KU Leuven currently has about 8.500 students, of which 1.400 are international students. The Faculty of Economics and Business (FEB) of the KU Leuven holds the EQUIS accreditation. This prestigious quality label affirms their place among the world's leading business schools and faculties.

info_about_university_raw: Université Laval is the oldest French-language university in North America. Inspired by excellence since 1663, UL has a clear vision for the future: to be one of the best universities in the world. UL is a comprehensive university boasting some 48,000 students—a quarter of them graduates—as well as 17 faculties, 60 departments and schools, and nearly 400 undergraduate and graduate programs in every field of knowledge.UL is also a leader in the area of research and innovation, with over 1,300 research professors divided among 250 teams and centres, and $300 million in annual research funding. UL also stands out for its vibrant academic and campus life. Determined to play a growing leadership role to help tackle key issues of our time, Université Laval has invested extensively in sustainable development and responsible resource management. It has been awarded prestigious “Sustainable Campus” certification by the Sierra Youth Coalition. Université Laval campus is one of the most striking in Quebec. It covers 1.2 sq. km and has over 30 pavilions, all linked by 10 km of underground walkways. It has a very large sports complex, library, bank, student computer center, Student Union Building (pub, restaurants, cafeteria, hair salon, bookstore, etc), and most public transportation routes stop on campus.

info_about_university_raw: The University of Calgary is young, innovative and forward-thinking, which has a lot to do with our surroundings. The Haskayne School of Business is closely linked to the global resource-based industries headquartered in western Canada: energy, mining, forestry, agribusiness, and tourism. It has played a pioneering role in integrating the management of environmental and social issues into the curriculum. In 2001, the Institute for Resource Industries and Sustainability Studies (IRIS) was established at the School, and houses a group of faculty from various disciplines and a group of Ph.D. students focused on resource industries and sustainable development management. The Haskayne School of Business is also a founding member of the University of Calgary’s interdisciplinary Institute for Sustainability, Energy and the Environment (ISEEE).

info_about_university_raw: Universidad de los Andes is a private research university located in the city centre of Bogotá, Colombia. It was founded on November 16th, 1948 and was the first private higher educational institution in Colombia that was nondenominational and independent from traditional political parties, as well as from social or economic power groups. The Universidad de los Andes’s state-of-the-art campus features an integrated library system, computer rooms, laboratories, and recreational and sporting areas, among other things. The School of Management is housed in a modern building equipped with all the technologies and comforts necessary for students’ learning. The campus of the Universidad de los Andes is found in an area of the city center known as Las Aguas, one of the oldest and most traditional sectors in Bogotá. Las Aguas is located in the district of La Candelaria, an area where important history of the capital dating back to colonial times is most densely concentrated. It is also the heart of many of the country’s most significant social, cultural, and political events. Its exceptional location at the foot of the Monserrate Mountain, an emblem of the city, ensures regular contact with nature and the tranquility needed to provide an environment suitable for study and research. Universidad de los Andes has 46 master’s programs and 32 undergraduate programs and a student population of 13.459 undergraduate students 2.744 master's students. Universidad de los Andes’ School of Management is within the one percent (1%) of business schools in the world that has the triple accreditation of AACSB, EQUIS, and AMBA. More information about the School of Management can be found here: https://administracion.uniandes.edu.co/index.php/en/

info_about_university_raw: American University in Cairo (AUC) was founded in 1919, and is a leading English-language, American-accredited, institution of higher education and center of intellectual, social and cultural life of the Arab world. The AUC campus is a so called “gated community”, located in one of the most secure residential suburbs of Cairo. info_about_university_raw: HEC Paris is a leading academic institution in Europe and worldwide, and is accredited by AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS. HEC Paris thereby holds the "triple crown" accreditation. HEC Paris’ mission is twofold: training the global leaders of tomorrow, and taking an active part in the production of knowledge on management. Created in 1881 by the Paris Chamber of Commerce and Industry, HEC Paris ambitions to train high potential individuals, capable of becoming architects of a responsible world. What makes HEC unique is its conviction shared by the HEC Community: knowledge determines the freedom and entrepreneurship required for a better world. This conviction is affirmed with our motto “The more you know, the more you dare”. HEC Paris is situated in Jouy-en-Josas, which is a commune in the Yvelines department in the Île-de-France region in north-central France. info_about_university_raw: Sciences Po is an international research university, both selective and open onto the world, ranking among the finest institutions in the fields of humanities and social sciences. Sciences Po has 13,000 students of whom 46% are international students, with 150 countries represented. Dijon campus Located in the region of Burgundy in a magnificent 19th century building, the Dijon campus was created in 2001 and is surrounded by gardens. It is a five-minute walk from the TGV train station and the city centre, in a quiet residential area with good public transport. More information about the Dijon campus can be found here and you can an insight into the campus through this video . Le Havre campus Since 2007, the city of Le Havre has been home to Sciences Po’s campus focusing on the Asia-Pacific region. Housed in a building overlooking the port, within a short distance of student residences and sports facilities, the Le Havre campus offers students a convenient and picturesque setting for their studies. More information about the Le Havre campus can be found here and you can get an insight into the campus through this video . Menton campus Opened in 2005, on the French riviera, Menton is Sciences Po’s southernmost campus. It sits in the heart of the city’s historic centre, in a nineteenth-century Italianate building facing out to the mediterranean. More information about the Menton campus can be found here and you can get an insight into the campus through this video . Nancy campus Established in the region of Lorraine in 2000, the Nancy campus is housed in a magnificent eighteenth-century building, the Hôtel des Missions Royales. It lies within walking distance of the famous Place Stanislas, a UNESCO world heritage site. More information about the Nancy campus can be found here and you can get an insight into the campus through this video . Poitiers campus Since 2001, the city of Poitiers has been home to Sciences Po’s campus focusing on Latin America, the Iberian Peninsula, and the Caribbean. Surrounded by the cobbled streets and Romanesque architecture for which Poitiers is known, the campus is located in the city centre, in an eighteenth-century listed building equipped with state-of-the-art study spaces. More information about the Poitiers campus can be found here and you can get an insight into the campus through this video . Reims campus The Reims campus provides an outstanding study environment, combining a superb architectural heritage (the campus is settled in a 17th century Jesuits' College) and ultra-modern facilities (fully renovated between 2009 and 2016). More information about the Reims campus can be found here and you can get an insight into the campus through this video .

The welcome team organizes different social activities. Trimester system, but there is a possibility to go on exchange for two trimesters and obtain full credit. You will therefore automatically be nominated to Toulouse Business School for two trimesters. Get a insight into Toulouse Business School by watching their Introduction video.

course_availability_raw: The university is multidisciplinary, but CBS students will primarily only be able to select courses within the fields of Business & Management, Economics, and among the International Affairs courses and electives. They offer a lot of courses in management but is not a business school as such. Students can select courses in French and/or English, as they prefer. Students should take all or most of their courses within the discipline, Business & Management or Economics, in which they have been nominated. Students can be allowed to take 1-2 course within one of the following disciplines as well: Political Sciences or Mathematics & Computer Sciences (it is not possible to take courses within Journalism and Law). Students can also take a French as a Foreign Language course (FLE courses) for credits, either as an intensive seminar in the beginning of the semester, or as a semester long course. CBS students should however check whether they are able to get such courses credit transferred or not. In case you cannot get a FLE courses approved for credit transfer, you can ask Paris Dauphine about taking it not-for-credits as well. Most courses are worth 6 ECTS each. It is in the fashionable 16th arondissement, not that far from t he Champs-Elysées, L'Arc de Triomphe and the Eiffel Tower, and also has a campus in La defence and in Tunesia. The university has approx. 10.000 students, of whom 25% are international, and 1100 are exchange students. Université Paris Dauphine has more than 30 student clubs and associations. They also have an integration week and a buddy program.

course_availability_raw: General information about courses: All exchange students are formally registered with Université Toulouse 1 Capitole (UT1), of which TSM is the management department. All incoming exchange students are guaranteed housing either in a Luiss Residence or in a private apartment with other students. For more information please see here .
course_availability_raw: All departments open to exchange students: Economics & Finance, Political Science (and Business & Management and Law). Students can mix different areas from different degrees in English. Please note that the number of bachelor courses offered in the fall semester is a bit limited. Examples of courses (more info can be found here ): Economics & Finance : Financial markets and institutions, information systems, macroeconomics, marketing, mathematical finance, money and banking, public economics, history of economic thought and policy etc. Political science: Comtemporary history, international law, international relations, methods of social research, microeconomics, political sociology, statistics, political economy of development etc. Department of Business and Management: Please note that course at the Department of Business and Management is also open to bachelor student, but there are none or only few courses available in the fall semester in English. Department of Law : With regards to courses within Law they are all on master level. You must ask your CBS study program if they will approve of you to take master courses within law. Most courses are worth 6-8 ECTS credits. LUISS allows bachelor students to follow Master courses as long as they have the required prerequisites, but students must make sure with their CBS Study Program that they will approve courses at Master level as part of their CBS degree. Please Note: Any list of courses might be subject to minor changes each year, and course availability is subject to student interest, enrollment and pre-requisites. CBS students should be aware that the course offer at the host university is not the same as at CBS.
additional_information_raw: Info on classes: Long academic periods, and exam until the end of February. In end June/July students pre-enroll in courses and can enroll for a total of 60 ECTS credits per semester. This provisional plan does not represent the student's final course choice. Final course enrollment will take place after their arrival, and students will be able to make all necessary changes then. Students have 2 weeks to try out classes (only drop, not add). With regards to exams: In the (very short) December session students are given only one opportunity to sit each exam. This has been arranged in order to take some pressure off the students from preparing all their exams in the ordinary January February examination period. It is well possible to sit them all by the end of this session but students should note that: Since they can pick exams from various majors, degree programs and levels, if they are unlucky two exams might happen to be scheduled at the same time; If they fail an exam, there is no problem at our end and they can retake it on the next available scheduled time, but it is going to be in January and February Given these variables, and depending on how many and which exams a student plans on taking, it may or may not be possible to take all exams before Christmas.
info_about_university_raw: LUISS Guido Carli is a private Italian university located in the heart of Rome. The University is EQUIS accredited and aims to achieve the highest levels of distinction in the development and transmission of scientific, technological, and classical knowledge and understanding. It comprises six campuses, all located nearby. University administration and academic offices are located throughout the six campuses. LUISS has around 8600 students in all, of them 300 are exchange students. Business is the largest program, app. 2500 out of 8600 students.

Courses are worth either 6 or 12 ECTS – students should be aware that some 12 ECTS courses are divided into two modules of 6 ECTS each, and that both modules must be passed to get the 12 ECTS for the course. Students can look for courses in the online course catalogue, which can be found here . You can find the ‘Guideline for course catalogue’ on how to use the course catalogue, and check any restrictions on course selection, here . Please note that course registration is not required for students to attend courses, but students must register for the courses they wish to attend the exam in, i.e., students can attend any course they wish, to try them out, but must register in the courses they wish to have credit transferred back to CBS. It is also possible for students to attend courses at the Venice International University (see more under Additional Information below). Please note: Any list of courses might be subject to minor changes each year, and course availability is subject to student interest, enrollment and pre-requisites. additional_information_raw: CBS students attending Ca’ Foscari on the exchange agreement between CBS and Ca’ Foscari also have the possibility to take some courses at Venice International University (VIU) , which is something unique in the academic world, namely a consortium of 20 universities from all over the world with an autonomous campus on the island of San Servolo, Venice, Italy. The focus areas of VIU are sustainability, innovation, globalization and global challenges, sciences and society, and humanities. For a list of courses, please check here and for how to enroll, please check here .
info_about_university_raw: Founded on August 6, 1868 as the Royal School of Commerce, Ca' Foscari was the first Italian institution to deal with advanced education in Business and Economics. The original main office is still found in the grand gothic palace “volta de canal” (on the bend of the Grand Canal), in the heart of Venice. Ca’ Foscari has a student body of approx. 23,000 of whom approx. 1/3 are international students and is EQUIS accredited.

Students normally select courses by the end of August and have the chance to modify their study plan during the Add/drop period in september. Students can take from a minimum of 2 up to a maximum of 5 courses. As the majority of Bocconi courses are worth 6 credits, usually the maximum numbers of credits exchange students can take is 30 (6 credits x 5 courses). However, some courses might be worth 7, 8, 9 or even 10 credits, meaning that students can reach more than 30 credits but still taking 5 courses. Students who wish to take all the exams by the December exam session (December 10-20, 2018), have to make sure that the classes they select have no exam conflict. If two final exams are scheduled on the same day and time, students can select both courses and sit the exams in different available sessions. Bocconi University has multiple exam sessions (Fall semester exam sessions: December and January/February). It is common that exams are written by hand at University of Bocconi. In case that is a problem for you, please notify University of Bocconi when you apply online for our exchange. info_about_university_raw: Hitotsubashi University is a national university corporation, and is the only university in Japan to specialize exclusively in the humanities and social sciences. Hitotsubashi has about 670 teaching staff members with approximately 4,400 students enrolled in undergraduate courses and 2,000 in graduate courses. There are some 580 international students, along with about 450 researchers from abroad. The academic organization of the University consists of four undergraduate faculties: Commerce and Management, Economics, Law, and Social Sciences. There are graduate schools in the same four fields, plus two additional programs: International Corporate Strategy and Language and Society. One of the campuses is located in the city of Kunitachi in the western part of the metropolitan area of Tokyo. Hitotsubashi is blessed with a wonderful main campus in Kunitachi, an oasis of color and peace amid the urban sprawl. Students, faculty, nearby residents and even a family of raccoons enjoy the extensive wooded areas. The main Kunitachi campus straddles the road from the station, and houses the University's central administration, professors' offices, the University Library, Kanematsu Auditorium, and numerous classrooms and faculty administration offices. The buildings, which are mostly in a Romanesque style, are well laid out and blend pleasantly with their rich, green surroundings. Sport is an important part of campus life, and Hitotsubashi has a variety of athletic facilities and sports fields on its three campuses as well as in the surrounding area. Students can take part in numerous activities including athletics, tennis, swimming, rugby, handball, hockey, martial arts and rowing. The facilities rival those of universities that specialize in physical education, and reflect the importance that the University attaches to physical as well as mental training. Hitotsubashi University emphasizes small-group class education, and one of the prominent characteristics is their seminar style approach. The seminar style approach keeps class sizes small and focuses on intense student-faculty interaction providing rich course content. Exchange students have a community assistant (like a buddy) who will help them out in the beginning of the semester.

info_about_university_raw: Keio has a proud history as Japan's very first private institution of higher learning, which dates back to the formation of a school for Dutch studies in 1858 in Edo, present-day Tokyo, by founder Yukichi Fukuzawa. Since the school's inception, the students of Keio have risen to the forefront of innovation in every imaginable academic field, emerging as social and economic leaders. In today's internationally interdependent world, Keio places great effort upon maintaining the finest teaching faculty and the highest standard of research and scholarship. Based on the knowledge and experience of their predecessors, today's Keio students strive to develop the leadership qualities that will enable them to make valuable contributions to tomorrow's society. The Faculty of Economics at Keio is one of Japan’s leading economics departments, and traces its history back to 1890, when Keio became the first Japanese institute of higher learning to establish a dedicated department for the theoretical and empirical investigation of economic issues. Since then, the study of economics has been pursued in a liberal, open-minded atmosphere, with the faculty committed to education and research of the highest caliber. Keio Economics alumni hold positions of leadership in politics, business, and academia, heading or serving on the boards of hundreds of publically listed companies, and many alumni are active at the highest levels of public service and government. Keio University has 6 different Campuses. Keio University is accredited by AACSB.

info_about_university_raw: Nagoya University of Commerce and Business was founded by Dr. Yuichi Kurimoto in 1953 and is recognized by the motto ‘Frontier Spirit’, symbolizing the strong spirit of being at the frontier of knowledge and communications. It is a private university established by the Kurimoto Educational Institute and situated in Nisshin, just outside Japan’s third-largest city, Nagoya. NUCB Undergraduate School has over 3,500 students, and 100 professors. The university has a strong commitment to excellence in case method teaching and research and has developed alliances with international institutions in Asia, Europe, North America, and Latin America. In 2006, NUCB Undergraduate School became the first AACSB-accredited undergraduate institution in Japan and has maintained it to date through high standards and continuous improvement. AACSB-accredited schools have better programs, better faculty, better students with higher overall GPAs, more international students, more employers that recruit from them, and graduates that receive better salaries. NUCB Business School, our Graduate School of Management, is the first and only Japanese business school to be accredited by AACSB, AMBA, and EQUIS, and thus, achieving the renowned Triple Crown. NUCB Business School is part of the PIM network as well. NUCB Undergraduate School offers an all-English degree program at the Bachelor level for undergraduate students through the Global BBA program. The goal of the program is to cultivate highly skilled professionals who develop a global perspective, a strong sense of ethics, and the ability to contribute positively to the international business community.

info_about_university_raw: Established in 2000, Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University (APU) is a 4-year university nestled in the mountains overlooking Beppu City in Oita Prefecture. Nearly 50% of students and faculty hail from overseas creating a vibrant international campus environment unparalleled in Japan. There are over 6000 undergraduate and graduate students from Japan and over 80 countries and regions. APU offers a dual language education in English and Japanese at the undergraduate level in the colleges of Asia Pacific Studies and International Management. Japanese language ability is not a prerequisite for admission to APU. However, many of the APU international graduates pursue employment or further study within Japan, and APU offers an intensive and systematic course of Japanese language to equip students with the language abilities they need for success in Japan. APU has a range of state-of-the-art amenities and equipment located in thirteen major buildings across the 416,000m² wide campus. These facilities serve as a base for academic interaction between Japan and the world while also providing students and faculty members a venue for study, research and various other activities. Ritsumeikan APU is AACSB accredited.

info_about_university_raw: Ritsumeikan has become an integrated academy with a rich culture of individuality and international awareness accommodating a total of 49,000 students. The current Ritsumeikan Academy has campuses in Kyoto, Shiga, Hokkaido, and Oita and encompasses two universities, four high schools, four junior high schools, and one primary school. Ritsumeikan fosters the learning and development of individual talents in order to nurture just and ethical global citizens. The Kinugasa Campus is located in northwestern Kyoto, a 1200 year old city rich in culture and art. Representative of Japanese learning and culture, Kyoto is a center for universities and university students. Kinugasa Campus is surrounded by such auspicious temples as Kinkakuji, Ryoanji, Ninnaji, and Tojiin, a suitably tranquil setting for research and learning. Kinugasa consists of six colleges (Law, Social Sciences, International Relations, Policy Science, Letters, and Image Arts and Sciences) and nine graduate schools (Law, Sociology, International Relations, Policy Science, Letters, Science for Human Services, Language Education & Information Science, Core Ethics & Frontier Sciences, and Image Arts and Sciences). The campus offers a comprehensive curriculum in the humanities and social sciences. The Inter-Faculty Institute for International Studies is also located at Kinugasa Campus. The Biwako-Kusatsu Campus is southeast of Lake Biwa. BKC houses six colleges (Economics, Business Administration, Science & Engineering, Information Science & Engineering, Life Sciences, and Pharmaceutical Sciences) and four graduate schools (Economics, Business Administration, Science & Engineering, and Technology Management). BKC also accommodates the Integrated Institute of Arts & Science. Kusatsu City is located in Shiga Prefecture northeast of Otsu City, at the southernmost edge of the Omi Valley. During the Edo Period Kusatsu prospered, being located at the crossroads of the great Tokaido and Nakasendo highways. Presently it is a center for machine technology and is the prefecture’s number one industrial city as well as the hub of real estate, economy and transit, south of Lake Biwa. Since 2015 there has emerged a new bigger campus between Kyoto and Osaka. The Business Administration and Political Science faculties are based here. It is a residential town called Ibaraki and is located 40 min from the current campus. There will be easy access to this campus.

info_about_university_raw: Waseda University is one of Japan's most prestigious private, co-educational institutions of higher learning. Waseda University was founded in 1882 by Shigenobu Okuma, later Prime Minister of Japan, with the aim of fostering contemporary Japanese leaders. It has since developed into a comprehensive university with now more than fifty thousand students and staff, comprising 13 Undergraduate Schools, 23 Graduate Schools, and other Research and Affiliated Institutes. The pedagogy and spirit embraced through Waseda's tradition and pride with a flexible and innovative mindset have ensured that Waseda stands firm at the forefront of Japanese education. Waseda University is located in the middle of Tokyo (Shinjuku) and it is the university in Japan that accepts the largest number of international students. Since Waseda University accepted its first exchange students in 1893, they have developed deep ties with countries around the world, especially in Asia. At present, Waseda University has research and student exchange agreements with more than 600 overseas universities and educational research institutions. Waseda currently accepts nearly 4,000 foreign students and dispatches 1,700 Waseda students overseas, including exchanges made outside the University-wide Agreements. In 2010, they began a phased implementation of English-language Bachelor's and Master's degree programs in five undergraduate schools and six graduate schools. There is another aspect of Waseda’s curriculum in which the university takes great pride: its clubs. Numbering over 700, Waseda’s clubs are grouped into five officially recognized types: athletic clubs (44 clubs), student associations (159 clubs), hobby clubs (347 clubs), regional student associations (22 clubs), and clubs recognized by individual schools (more than 100 clubs). It is said that if unofficial organizations are included, the number of university clubs exceeds 2,000. In fact, there are so many clubs that it is said that there is no topic for which a club has not been formed. All of these organizations offer ample opportunities for anyone with enthusiasm to shine. Also, Waseda University’s tradition as a leader in Japan’s collegiate sports is alive and well. Waseda’s athletes are electrifying not only the collegiate sports world but Japan’s entire sports scene.

info_about_university_raw: Monash University, established in 1961, is Australia's largest university with more than 55,000 students. Monash was the first foreign university to establish a campus in Malaysia. The Sunway Campus is located in the township Bandar Sunway just outside of the metropolitan capital city of Kuala Lumpur. The Sunway campus welcomes more than 150 exchange students annually and about 30% percent of the student body is international. The Sunway campus of Monash University is an example of transnational education. Because they are a campus of Monash University, all staff and students are part of a global academy with an international reputation for excellence in teaching and research. Studying or working at Monash Sunway is a dynamic, international experience. The community of scholars is supported by collegial processes and comprehensive first-class infrastructure. While they are firmly engaged in Malaysia and the region, their focus is also relentlessly global, so Monash graduates emerge ready to transform the world around them. The Faculty of Business and Economics is EQUIS, AACSB and AMBA accredited (the so-called Triple Crown Accreditation) and the university is a member of the Group of Eight - a coalition of Australian top research intensive universities.

info_about_university_raw: The University of Malaya is the oldest and one of the most prestigious learning institutions in Malaysia. UM is the foremost and premier Research University (RU) in Malaysia. It is a multidisciplinary RU that has more than 27,000 students and 1700 academic staff with 17 faculties and research centres that covers the whole spectrum of learning from the Arts, Sciences and Humanities. The university's beginning at the Kuala Lumpur campus dates back to 1959 and thus far has a huge alumni of over 100,000, among them renowned and illustrious personalities and leaders in various fields. UM is the first choice of Malaysia's top students and the international student population comes from more than 80 different countries. The beautiful 900-acre campus lies within the heart of Kuala Lumpur city and this strategic location is truly an advantage for UM's international academic staff and visitors. The University of Malaya, being a comprehensive, research-intensive university, confers degrees in a large variety of academic programmes at the Bachelors, Masters and PhD levels. The university also offers joint PhD degrees with international partner universities such as the University of Sydney, University of Melbourne, University of Nottingham, Imperial College London, and the Consortium of Presidents of Universities (CPU) in France. The Residential Halls are providing facilities such as game courts, reading rooms, grocery shops, cyber cafes and computer labs. University of Malaya is accredited by AMBA.

housing_raw: All exchange and study abroad students are required to live in university housing (on-campus). Normally, housing is based on double occupancy and every effort is made to pair international students with a Moroccan counterpart. Single rooms are not available. Housing for a married couple provided that both are students is possible but available on a case by case basis. Students with children cannot be accommodated. Students apply for housing online in June/July (you will receive information from the university).
course_availability_raw: Examples of courses: Arabic as a foreign language (ARA) Arabic for native speakers (ARB) Islamic Art and Architecture History of the Arab World North African Politics and Government History of North Africa and Middle East in the 20th Century Arab Society Middle Eastern Politics Women in Culture and the Media Women in Society and Politics Sex, Gender and Politics Women and Economic Development Economic Geography Political Geography Politics in the Developing World Introduction to the European Union Social Statistics Media and Development Economic Development in the Middle East and North Africa Political Anthropology Theories & Models of International Relations History and Culture of the Berbers Issues in the Multi-Cultural Workplace Comparative Accounting Systems Macroeconomics International Marketing International Trade International Finance International Marketing International Law Seminar in International Management Computer Science Chemistry Biology Electric Circuits Linear Algebra Materials Science Find more info in the factsheet at the bottom of this page. Here you can also find a course list and the description of the courses. After nomination to Al Akhawayn you will be contacted to select courses. Often you will have to select main classes and alternative classes, as there is an add-drop period at the beginning of the semester. When selecting courses, it is important that you make sure that you have the right pre-requisites. additional_information_raw: International students should arrive at AUI in time to take part in the new student orientation program (and have to pay a fee). International student handbook can be found here . The university has a Pick-up service from either Fez airport or train station for when you arrive in Morocco. More detials can be found in the Student Handbook. Attendance is compulsory in all classes. Missing five/seven or more classes without an excused absence will lead to the grade “withdraw failing” (WF). Full details are in the Student Handbook. Please note: Female students should be aware that social norms regarding the relationship between the sexes are very different from Denmark. E.g. walking alone in the streets can be uncomfortable, and you should be more aware of the signals you send, when you are around local males.
info_about_university_raw: Inaugurated in 1995 by the late King Hassan II of Morocco and the late King Fahd of Saudi Arabia, Al Akhawayn University redefines the classic American liberal arts educational experience on an architecturally stunning modern campus amidst the beauty of Morocco's Middle Atlas Mountains.< the university has approx. 2000 students, and is an English medium of instruction institution and follows a North American Curriculum: normal course load = 15 credits (5 courses). You can check out their YouTube channel here , where you can get an insight into studying/life at Al Akhawayn University.
visa_raw: There are no visa requirements prior to arrival for citizens of the USA, Canada, Japan, Korea or countries of Western Europe who all may initially enter Morocco as tourists. Students from outside the above mentioned areas must acquire a student visa in order to enter Morocco. All international students are required to apply for residency even if only at AUI for a semester because the status is that of a student and not a tourist. Students will begin the residency application procedure during the orientation period. This requires several forms to be completed, special identity size photos taken locally upon arrival and copies of the student's passport to be notarized with local authorities. This cost will be 200 MAD, around $ 20.

limitations_raw: Note that the normal workload per trimester at RSM is 20 ECTS, but students can be allowed to take up to 30 ECTS, however it is recommended to not take more than 24 ECTS.
course_availability_raw: CBS bachelor students have access to courses offered by Rotterdam School of Management. Exchange students have access to courses from the bachelor curriculum and can take courses from all three years of the bachelor program – however it is recommended that students make sure that the level correspond to being a 3rd year bachelor student at CBS. For more information about courses, please check at the end of this page or here . Besides taking “regular” courses, bachelor students also have the option of taking 1 minor (worth 15 ECTS) during the fall - this is optional though. For more information about minors, please check at the end of this page or here . Please note: Any list of courses might be subject to minor changes each year, and course availability is subject to student interest, enrollment and pre-requisites. CBS students should be aware that the course offer at the host university is not the same as at CBS.
program_information_raw: In the fall term, students will be following courses in different blocks: block 1 and 2 (1 year bachelor level courses) block 5 and 6 (2 year bachelor level courses) block 9 and 10 (3 year bachelor level - minor and electives) The courses vary in ECTS per course (usually between 3 and 5 ECTS per course). Whereas a minor consist of 15 ECTS. RSM runs on a block structure on the bachelor program, and the recommended workload for a term is 20-24 ECTS. However, it is possible to take 30 ECTS during your exchange at RSM.
info_about_university_raw: Rotterdam School of Management is one of a select group of schools with Triple Crown accreditation from EQUIS, AACSB, and the Association of MBA’s. In the 2011 meta-ranking, the Financial Times placed RSM amongst the top 10 schools in Europe. RSM’s MBA programme appears in the European top 15. RSM is a member of the Community of European Management Schools (CEMS), and of the Partnership in International Management (PIM).

course_availability_raw: CBS students only have access to courses offered by the Maastricht University School of Business and Economics (SBE). The semesters are divided into 3 periods each, where students can take a maximum of 2 courses in each of the first and second period of each semester (= 4 courses in total of maximum 26 ECTS) + take one skill training course in the third period (= 4 ECTS). Please note that most courses are worth 6.5 ECTS, but some are only worth 5 ECTS, so please check carefully to make sure that you get enough ECTS for the semester. additional_information_raw: Courses at Maastricht University are challenging and reflect real-life challenges faced in business today. Its unique problem-based learning model encourages students to work collaboratively to analyse cases, develop innovative approaches, and identify unique methods for seeking solutions.
info_about_university_raw: Maastricht University is highly regarded in Europe for its unique teaching style and high-quality research. For several years now, a number of national surveys have ranked consistently Maastricht University, and more specifically, the Maastricht University School of Business and Economics (SBE) as the best in terms of education and research. Moreover, SBE has been awarded three prestigious accreditations, resulting in the so-called Triple Crown accreditation. Only 1% of the business schools worldwide have this Triple Crown, meaning that the school is amongst a very select group of institutions. It is a distinctly international institution with a student population consisting of over 66 nationalities. Of the total of 3750 bachelor and master students more than 1500 (40%) have a foreign background. Additionally, the School yearly welcomes about 400 exchange students from its 135 partner universities worldwide. Get a insight into Maastricht University School of Business and Economics by watching their promotion video.

info_about_university_raw: Radboud University is a leading research university located in the southeast of the Netherlands. Established in 1923, the university is home to more than 24,000 students and offers over 100 study programmes, including a wide range of English-taught bachelor’s and master’s programmes. With its green, compact campus and international community, Radboud University provides an inspiring environment where students and researchers work together to address the challenges of today’s world. The Nijmegen School of Management is one of Radboud University’s seven faculties. It brings together disciplines such as Business Administration, Economics, Public Administration, Political Science, and Environmental Governance. The faculty is dedicated to understanding complex social issues and promoting sustainable and ethical management practices, preparing students to become responsible leaders in an interconnected world. Get a insight into the Nijmegen School of Management and Radboud University by watching this welcome video .

additional_information_raw: Tilburg University has 14 international student organizations catering to a variety of interests, for example the International Exchange Erasmus Student Network. The School of Economics and Management has its own study association ‘Asset’ which you can join. Excellent sports facilities The state-of-the-art Sports Center offers a wide variety of sports and exercise facilities at all levels. The Center has two large sports halls, fitness rooms, a dedicated weight-training area, squash courts and a sauna. The outdoor facilities include a semi-water-based hockey pitch, six tennis courts and a beach volleyball pitch, among others. The Sports Center offers over 45 sports activities, including zumba, indoor cycling, table tennis and yoga. Join them individually or as a member of one of the sports associations.
info_about_university_raw: Tilburg University is a thriving university specializing in Social Sciences and Arts & Humanities. Social connection, academic excellence, and a strong campus feeling are at the heart of the education experience at Tilburg University. The green campus offers an attractive base for fostering an international community where students and teachers can inspire and challenge each other. Tilburg University consists of five different schools: Economics & Management, Law, Social and Behavioral Sciences, Humanities and Digital Sciences, and Theology. Tilburg University belongs to the best 2% of the world’s universities (according to three of the most renowned university rankings (THE, ARWU, and QS)). Tilburg Campus life: With a green campus designed to be fast and easy to navigate, you will be able to stroll between the library and your lecture hall or your favorite café in no time. All university buildings are within walking distance from each other, and are set amongst landscaped gardens and open green spaces. Tilburg campus is home to over 17,000 students. Please, be informed that Utrecht University does not own any accommodation for students. However, the university has an agreement with SSH Short Stay, a local housing corporation that offers temporary furnished housing. They reserve a range of furnished accommodation especially for international students of Utrecht University. Availability is limited and NOT guaranteed! Utrecht strongly urge all exchange students to register at Short Stay Solutions (www.sshxl.nl) since this is the only accommodation option the university can help and assist you with.

Every year, approximately 2.000 international students come to Utrecht University to take part in English-taught degree programmes and other courses. With some 125 nationalities working and studying closely together, students learn to work in an international environment from the start - essential for scientists and scholars in an increasingly globalised world. Utrecht University is situated at three different locations in Utrecht. In the charming, historic city centre of Utrecht you will find the Faculty of Humanities and the Faculty of Law, Economics & Governance.

housing_raw: On-campus housing is available. AUT’s lease of the Wellesley Student Apartments (WSA) will come to an end on 31 December 2024. From the start of 2025, the only AUT accommodation option available to students in the city will be Te Āhuru Mayoral Drive Student Accommodation. Te Āhuru Mayoral Drive Student Accommodation is a modern and purpose-built facility located across the street from the AUT City Campus. Offering studio-style living, residents at Te Āhuru Mayoral Drive Student Accommodation have their own private bedroom, bathroom, kitchenette and study area. Residents also have access to commercial and self-use kitchens and dining facilities, study facilities, and laundry facilities. Additionally, AUT’s Te Āhuru Recreation Centre is located in the same building, offering convenient access to residents to all the recreation centre has to offer.
course_availability_raw: Access to courses within the Bachelor of Business (all majors) at the Faculty of Business, Economics and Law. Also access to courses at the Faculty of Culture & Society and Faculty of Māori and indigenous development - Te Ara Poutama. Any list of courses might be subject to minor changes each year, and course availability is subject to student interest, enrollment and pre-requisites. CBS students should be aware that the course offer at the host university is not the same as at CBS.
program_information_raw: Incoming exchange students to the AUT Business School has access to the following programmes: Bachelor of Business (BBus) Bachelor of Business majors are: Accounting, Advertising, Business Information Systems, Design, Economics, Finance, Human Resource Management and Employment Relations, International Business, Management, Marketing, Retailing, Sales, Sustainable Enterprise and Tourism. Students can also take courses within the Faculty of Culture and Society and the Faculty of Māori and indigenous development - Te Ara Poutama.
additional_information_raw: Each semester AUT University provides a number of student events and student support services that every exchange student has access to. There are also a number of events that are offered only to International, Study Abroad and Exchange students. These include: International Student Orientation before semester, Welcome party for all Study Abroad and exchange students, International Student Noho Marae weekend. The AUT Business School also has a personal orientation session and a welcome lunch for incoming business exchange students. You can find the AUT exchange fact sheet and more info here
info_about_university_raw: AUT is New Zealand’s newest university but their history in industry-relevant education is over 110 years old. AUT is home to over 26,000 students at across three campuses in: Auckland, Manukau and North Shore. The following faculties are located at the City Campus: Business and Law, Culture and Society, Design and Creative Technologies, Health and Environmental Sciences and Te Ara Poutama (Maori Development). At the Business School, you will find more than 5,000 students. The AUT Business School is known in New Zealand and internationally for high quality graduates, the positive impact of its research and meaningful engagements with business and the broader community. Their v alues are: 1. Rigorous, relevant and engaging education, 2. Research that matters, 3. Locally-grounded, globally connected. The AUT Business School has over 30 professional staff leading the curriculum and who are engaged in research that matters to their stakeholders. AUT has research strengths across all major business fields but also have interdisciplinary research and research on business pedagogy. The academic staff are capable, enthusiastic teachers and researchers with backgrounds in academia and/or professional practice. Strong links with industry and professorial bodies is a defining characteristic of the AUT Business School and this ensures that the curriculum remains current and reflects the needs of contemporary business. CBS exchange students will be taking courses at the City Campus. There are many nice facilities at the City campus: Library – 4 floors, Art galleries, Cafés, restaurants and bars, Fitness centre and gymnasium and it is close to the city center. There is a shuttle bus to AUT North Shore campus. AUT's Business School is AACSB and EQUIS accredited.

Lincoln University is ranked in the top 500 by QS World Rankings and is ranked in the top 100 in the world for agricultural programmes. info_about_university_raw: University of Canterbury is a highly ranked world class university and the first New Zealand university to receive the prestigious QS five-star ranking for overall excellence. The UC Business School holds ‘Triple-Crown’ accreditation by AMBA, EQUIS, and AACSB, putting it in the top 1% of business schools worldwide. UC’s academic staff are well known in their fields and often write the textbooks you will study. UC also brings in academics from around the world, including Oxford and Cambridge, via their staff exchange programme. UC is home to over 40 recognised research centres, institutes, and hubs and is an important research university in Australasia. Over 100 different subjects are offered across 7 Faculties (Arts, Business, Education, Engineering, Health, Law, and Science). UC offers a comprehensive range of courses, including several that you’re unlikely to come across at home - such as Māori language and culture, Antarctic Studies and courses in New Zealand and Pacific literature, history and politics. There are more than 160 student clubs at UC, covering almost every interest imaginable from sports, politics and international communities through to performing arts and social groups. UC Sport also has group fitness, sport courts, social sport and full weights and cardio options.

Rent fees include electricity, internet, bed linen, kitchen equipment, UniFlats community events and the services of the University Flats. Flatting expenses are shared with the other students in the flat and are not included in the rent.

info_about_university_raw: The University of Otago is New Zealand's oldest university, founded in 1869. It has earned an international reputation for the quality of its research and teaching. Teaching at Otago is closely related to scholarly research, with the result that most teaching is undertaken by academics at the forefront of relevant knowledge. University of Otago is situated in the charming town Dunedin on the South Island. There is a vibrant student atmosphere in the city and a lot of things to see and do in the area. As a student at New Zealand's oldest university you will become part of a unique educational experience. Otago's attractive campus is a mixture of historic and modern buildings located in the centre of Dunedin. The campus is a short walk from the city's central shopping and services. Otago students rate its campus lifestyle as one of its strongest attractions. The students live as a community immediately around the campus area in student Colleges of Residence or self-catering flats. University of Otago is part of PIM (Partnership in International Management), which is a consortium of leading international business schools, founded in 1973 The campus is smoke free. The policy covers all vehicles, buildings and grounds owned or leased by the University of Otago. This policy will also include Residential Colleges and University Flats.

This means that students may not be placed in one of their initial choices for accommodation. It is therefore very important to submit the accommodation application and application fee by the deadline if you want VUW to help you find a place to stay. In general it is easier to find a place to stay on campus in the semester running from July to November.

The courses within commercial law are especially interesting for our 'HA.jur' students.
additional_information_raw: Arriving in a new city and at a new university can be overwhelming. It can also be exciting. A great way to start, meet new people and find your way around is to sign up for a Victoria International Buddy. Your buddy will welcome you to campus, help you with information about the university and local customs and provide advice about flatting and living in Wellington. Most of all, your buddy will be a friendly face who is keen to learn about you. All local buddies receive support training to assist in their role.
info_about_university_raw: VUW is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in New Zealand and was founded in 1897. The University is New Zealand's leading research and development centre in many key international growth areas including bioscience, Earth processes, materials science, built environments, business, law, creative research, and policy, governance and society. VUW has seven faculties and is home to over 22,000 students including around 3,000 international students. Victoria has 4 main campuses, three of which are all within 15 minutes walk from each other in the city, in the midst of the cafes, galleries, and shops. Victoria has introduced the Victoria International Leadership Programme. As an exchange student at VUW, you can also participate. Read more about it at https://www.victoria.ac.nz/home/study/leadership-programmes/vilp Wellington's School of Business and Government is EQUIS, AMBA and AACSB accredited. Only few business schools in the world hold the so-called triple crown accreditation. CBS is also one of them.

When students apply for Universidade Católica Portuguesa (to the university), they must apply for either Business or Economics in order to get enrolled in the university (but can take courses from both). Bachelor students: The bachelor program consists of semesters (whereas the master program consists of trimesters). For BA students elective courses are taught in English and core courses in Portuguese. They can study within Business and Economics. Normally they take 5 courses. For more info, please check the fact sheet below. Example of courses: Microeconomics Statistics II Finance I Marketing Economic History Organizational Behavior Econometrics Multivariate Statistics Strategy Management Control Systems International Economics Ethics and Social Responsibility Economic Analysis of Social Policies Economic of Regulation Macroeconomic Policy Capital Markets and Institutions Bank Management Product and Costumer Management Marketing in the New Era Topics in Marketing Global Marketing Management Taxation in Portugal Data Management Tools Organizational Sociology Strategic Management of Innovation Government and Business Contemporary Political Thought: Europe in the 20th Century Behavioral Decision Making Leadership in Organizations Leadership in Business Model Innovation Business and Its Environment Economic Policy in the European Union Entrepreneurship Bachelor students must take more than 50% of their courses at the School of Business and Economics. Beyond that they are also allowed to take courses at: H uman Sciences Faculty Political Sciences Institute Law School Please note: It's the student's responsibiliy to contact The International Offices at these other Faculties to enquire about their course offer in English. Since all Faculties of Universidade Católica Portuguesa have absence control and that overlapping of schedule is not allowed, students have to confirm that all their courses from the different Faculties are compatible, and as all Faculties have different enrollment/assessment procedures/rules and different academic calendars it is students' responsibility to consider this too. Please have in mind that course enrolment is made on a “first-come, first-served” policy. As such, Catolica Lisbon do not guarantee slots in courses. additional_information_raw: Bachelor students can take 30 ECTS credits. If bachelor students have started classes that they cannot get approved at CBS or dislikes, they can still drop the courses, but they cannot add a new course. Attendance to classes is mandatory and there is have absence control. As such, overlapping of schedule is not allowed.
